required.check: DataIntersection contract: `transform()` is the only CTL entry point and runs once per matched pair (`$in.0` = yesterday, `$in.1` = today); it returns an emit value (OK, 0, 1 or ALL all emit) for a notice and SKIP to suppress, and departures/arrivals (ports 0 and 2) are left to the component without CTL handling.
required.rationale: A solution that tries to route one-sided rows itself or returns a non-emit code for a changed pair loses notices.

required.check: Tier comparison maps null, empty and whitespace-only tier_txt to the same absent value before comparing (e.g. `isnull(s) ? "" : upperCase(trim(s))`, or `isBlank(s)` → "").
required.rationale: `upperCase(trim(null))` stays null while `""` stays empty, so the null-vs-empty pair (key A) falsely reports TIER.

required.check: For non-blank tiers the comparison uses `upperCase(trim(...))` on both sides, so ` silver ` and `SILVER` agree.
required.rationale: Raw comparison reports TIER for whitespace/case-only differences that the spec says are equal.

required.check: interests_txt is split on ";" and every token is trimmed and upper-cased before comparison; punctuation inside a token (e.g. BAD:DATE) is kept as part of the name.
required.rationale: Comparing raw text makes `BAD:DATE` vs `bad:date` (key C) a spurious INTERESTS change.

required.check: Null interests_txt and blank tokens both give the empty set: null is guarded before `split` (or mapped to ""), and tokens that are empty after trimming are discarded, so null and " ; " compare equal.
required.rationale: Keeping blank tokens or splitting null makes the null vs " ; " pair (key A) report INTERESTS or fail.

required.check: The two token collections are compared as sets: repeated tokens are ignored and order does not matter (e.g. de-duplicate then `sort` both lists and compare, compare joined sorted strings, or check mutual containment with `in`/`containsValue`).
required.rationale: List or string equality without de-duplication and ordering treats `SHOE;HAT` vs `hat;shoe;shoe` as changed.

required.check: Credit nulls: when exactly one credit_limit is null the pair has a CREDIT change, when both are null there is none, and the subtraction is only evaluated when both are non-null.
required.rationale: Computing `abs(a-b)` with a null operand throws or mis-classifies the one-null case.

required.check: When both credit_limit values are present, CREDIT is set iff `abs(old - new) >= 0.05` (inclusive, e.g. compared with `0.05D`), on the unrounded decimal difference, so 2.00→2.05 changes and 1.00→1.04 does not.
required.rationale: Using `>` or rounding first misses the exact-boundary 2.00→2.05 change on key C.

required.check: consent_until is compared as a full date-time with null-safe inequality (`!=`/`==` are null-safe in CTL2, or explicit null handling): both null agree, null vs a date differs, and a time-only difference (00:00:00 vs 00:00:01) is a change; no truncation to the day or date-only formatting.
required.rationale: Comparing day strings or treating midnight as missing loses the 00:00:00→00:00:01 CONSENT change on key C.

required.check: change_names lists only the changed comparisons in the fixed order TIER, INTERESTS, CREDIT, CONSENT, joined with "," and no spaces or trailing comma (`join(",", list)` or equivalent concatenation), built fresh for each pair.
required.rationale: Wrong order or separators ("CREDIT, CONSENT", trailing comma) break the exact change_names value.

required.check: A pair with no semantic change returns SKIP (no notice); a changed pair sets notice_kind = "NOTICE" and is emitted.
required.rationale: Emitting every match ignores the unchanged A pair the spec suppresses.

required.check: The notice copies the raw fields from today's record `$in.1` (`$out.0.* = $in.1.*` or per-field from `$in.1`), keeping the original tier_txt and interests_txt text rather than the normalised forms, and never takes yesterday's (`$in.0`) context.
required.rationale: Copying `$in.0` or writing the canonical set into interests_txt corrupts the delivered record (expected `SHOE;hat`, source_row 7).

forbidden.check: Writes the notice to `$out.1` or `$out.2` (DataIntersection CTL has only the internal `$out.0`, delivered on physical port 1; writing `$out.1` fails at graph init).
forbidden.rationale: Live runs show the graph does not start when CTL writes `$out.1`.

forbidden.check: Returns STOP (or another negative non-SKIP code) from `transform()`; STOP makes the DataIntersection fail with an error.
forbidden.rationale: Live run 17993 shows STOP terminates the graph with an error instead of dropping the pair.

forbidden.check: Filters repeated business_ref matches with a seen-key list or previous-key variable, so the second B pair produces no notice.
forbidden.rationale: The spec requires every Cartesian pair of duplicate keys to be compared; the fixture expects two B notices.

T54.notes: Dropped old T54.8 (Cartesian pairs/fresh reasons): any per-call local list satisfies it; the seen-key filter is kept as forbidden F3. Prompt clause 8 says 'Two old B rows and one new B row' and the fixture matches (2 old, 1 new); reviewer noted no reversed-order unchanged interest pair in the fixture, so item .6's order-independence is checked by reading only. 0.05 (number literal) vs 0.05D at the exact boundary is unverified at runtime; the item accepts any inclusive >= 0.05 decimal comparison.

required.check: ExtMergeJoin FULL_OUTER contract: one `transform()` is called for every matched pair and for every one-sided record (the absent side's fields are null), writes `$out.0` and returns OK/0/ALL to emit or SKIP to omit.
required.rationale: Assuming one-sided records bypass the transform (or need separate callbacks) loses WAITING/UNPLANNED rows.

required.check: Side presence is detected from something that is null only for an absent side: the non-nullable `business_ref` of that side (`isnull($in.0.business_ref)`), or record-level `isnull($in.N)` / `$in.N == null`; never from a nullable amount or text field.
required.rationale: Testing `isnull($in.0.expected_amount)` turns the present invoice G (null amount) into a bank-only UNPLANNED row instead of EXPECTED_NULL.

required.check: Context comes from the invoice (`$in.0`) whenever it is present, including matched pairs, and from the bank (`$in.1`) only when the invoice is absent (e.g. `$out.0.* = $in.0.*` in one branch, `$out.0.* = $in.1.*` in the other), copying every context field verbatim.
required.rationale: Copying both sides in sequence lets the bank overwrite the invoice context on matched rows (expected source_row 3, not 8).

required.check: A present bank row whose settlement_state is exactly "VOID" (case-sensitive `==`, no trim) gets settled amount 0 and its settled_txt is neither validated nor parsed.
required.rationale: Validating first turns VOID row E (settled_txt '2025-02-30') into an AMOUNT_TEXT repair instead of a balanced omitted pair.

required.check: For non-VOID bank rows, the trimmed settled_txt must fully match an optional minus, 1–10 ASCII digits and an optional '.' with 1–2 digits (e.g. `~= "-?[0-9]{1,10}(\\.[0-9]{1,2})?"`) before `str2decimal`; plus sign, exponent (1e2), commas and longer fractions fail.
required.rationale: `str2decimal` accepts forms like '1e2' that the spec rejects, so parsing first misses the AMOUNT_TEXT repair on row C.

required.check: A null or blank (after trim) settled_txt on a present non-VOID bank row is AMOUNT_TEXT, handled without calling `str2decimal` on it (`str2decimal("")` throws).
required.rationale: Treating null/blank text as zero or passing it to str2decimal either hides a repair or aborts the graph.

required.check: A present invoice with null expected_amount (and no AMOUNT_TEXT) becomes REPAIR with error_reason EXPECTED_NULL; no numeric default is substituted.
required.rationale: `nvl(expected_amount, 0)` turns invoice G into an UNPLANNED/WAITING follow-up.

required.check: AMOUNT_TEXT takes precedence over EXPECTED_NULL when a pair has both a malformed bank amount and a null invoice amount.
required.rationale: Checking the invoice first gives row C the wrong error_reason.

required.check: Repair rows set reconcile_kind "REPAIR", the selected error_reason, and settled_amount and remaining_amount null (expected_amount is not graded on repair rows: invoice value, null or 0 are all accepted).
required.rationale: Leaving computed quantities on a repair row makes it look like a valid settlement.

required.check: Valid rows use 0 for an absent side's amount (missing invoice → expected 0, missing bank → settled 0), compute remaining_amount = expected − settled in decimal, write all three quantities, and set error_reason to "".
required.rationale: Leaving the absent-side amount null makes remaining_amount null on WAITING/UNPLANNED rows.

required.check: A valid matched pair with remaining_amount == 0 is omitted (SKIP), while one-sided rows are emitted even when their amount is zero.
required.rationale: Skipping on zero regardless of sides drops invoice-only I (0.00) and bank-only B (0).

required.check: reconcile_kind for follow-ups: invoice-only WAITING, bank-only UNPLANNED, matched remaining > 0 SHORT, remaining < 0 EXCESS (negative amounts are legitimate, e.g. −2.00 vs −3.00 → +1.00 SHORT).
required.rationale: Swapping the sign test or the one-sided labels mislabels rows A, B, F and H.

forbidden.check: Calls `str2decimal` (or `str2double`) on settled_txt before the full-shape check, so blank text throws or malformed text is silently accepted or converted to zero.
forbidden.rationale: The spec requires a defined AMOUNT_TEXT repair, not an exception or a silent value.

forbidden.check: Uses `number`/double arithmetic (e.g. `str2double`, number variables) for expected, settled or remaining amounts.
forbidden.rationale: The spec requires exact decimal subtraction; doubles introduce representation error in the ledger amounts.

T55.notes: Old T55.9 duplicated .6/.7 and was folded into items .2/.7/.11. expected_amount on a bank-only REPAIR row is unspecified by the prompt (reference writes 0; null is equally defensible) — item .9 does not grade it; consider stating it in the prompt. Record-level `isnull($in.N)` / `$in.N == null` for absent-side detection is accepted but not verified by a live run.

required.check: Denormalizer contract: `append()` runs for every record of the group and updates the saved winner; `transform()` runs once per group and writes the saved winner plus winner_complete and versions_seen to `$out.0` (returning OK).
required.rationale: Building the winner in transform() from `$in.0` (the last record) ignores every earlier candidate.

required.check: A version is complete only if legal_nm, tax_country and payment_iban are each non-null and non-blank after trimming (e.g. `!isBlank(x)`, `x != null && trim(x) != ""`, or `trim(nvl(x,"")) != ""`); nonblank text such as BAD:DATE counts as present and nothing is parsed.
required.rationale: Missing the blank/empty case marks supplier B's '' or ' ' legal_nm as complete.

required.check: A complete candidate beats an incomplete current winner regardless of revision_at or revision_no, and an incomplete candidate never replaces a complete winner.
required.rationale: Ranking by recency first picks A's incomplete 2026 row over the complete 1960 row.

required.check: Within equal quality, a non-null revision_at beats a null one, including a pre-epoch value such as 1960-01-01 (no comparison against epoch/zero to mean 'missing').
required.rationale: Treating dates before 1970 or at midnight as missing reverses the real-vs-null rule.

required.check: When both revision_at values are non-null, the later full date-time wins (`>` on the date values, not on formatted strings or date parts).
required.rationale: Comparing only the date part ignores later same-day revisions.

required.check: When the timestamps are equal, including null vs null (null-safe `==`), the greater revision_no wins.
required.rationale: A non-null-safe comparison skips the revision_no tiebreak for suppliers B and D (expected rows 5 and 9).

required.check: An exact tie (same quality, same revision_at, same revision_no) keeps the earlier-arriving row: replacement uses strict comparisons (`>`), not `>=`.
required.rationale: Using >= lets row 3 replace row 1 for supplier A, and row 6 replace row 5 for B.

required.check: The winner's fields are all saved from the same source record at the moment it becomes the winner — either per-field global variables or a record variable (e.g. `Candidate w; w.* = $in.0.*;` then `$out.0.* = w.*`) — and all 18 input fields are written from that saved record.
required.rationale: Saving only the ranking fields and copying the rest from another record builds a version that never existed.

required.check: Saved values are the raw field values: whitespace in legal_nm/tax_country/payment_iban (' L ', ' IBAN ') and the null vs empty distinction are preserved (trim is used only for classification).
required.rationale: Storing trimmed values changes the delivered winner text.

required.check: versions_seen counts every record of the group, including duplicates and losing candidates.
required.rationale: Counting only replacements or distinct revisions gives A=1 instead of 3.

required.check: winner_complete is the completeness of the selected record (saved together with it), not of the last record or 'any complete seen'.
required.rationale: Using the last record's quality reports A's winner as incomplete.

required.check: Per-group state — the first-candidate flag/counter, saved quality and versions_seen — is reset for the next key, in `clean()` or at the end of `transform()` (equivalent in the Denormalizer).
required.rationale: Without the reset, group B is compared against A's complete winner and its count continues from 3.

forbidden.check: Detects 'no winner yet' by testing a bare-declared winner variable with `== null`/`isnull()` or against epoch/0/"" (declared variables start at epoch/0/"", never null), instead of an explicit flag, counter or index.
forbidden.rationale: With null revision_at and revision_no 1 the sentinel never fires or fires wrongly, so the first version is not taken as candidate.

forbidden.check: Writes the winner to `$out.0` inside `append()` and relies on that for output (assignments to `$out.0` in append() have no effect).
forbidden.rationale: The emitted record would carry no winner values.

T56.notes: Prompt clause 8 previously named a 'dob' field (reviewer); current prompt text does not, nothing to fix in the rubric. The first-candidate requirement (clause 6) is enforced through F1 rather than a mirrored required item.

required.check: Rollup contract: all five functions are defined; `updateGroup` returns true so `updateTransform(counter, acc)` runs after each record, and like `transform(counter, acc)` it is called with counter 0, 1, … until it returns SKIP — so each emits its record at counter 0 and returns SKIP for counter > 0; `updateTransform` returns 0 (port 0) and the group `transform` returns 1 (port 1).
required.rationale: Without SKIP at counter > 0 the function is called again and duplicates the row; returning the wrong port mixes the streams.

required.check: A receipt_id is usable only if non-null and non-blank after trimming (e.g. `!isBlank(id)` or `id != null && trim(id) != ""`); unusable ids get INVALID and are not added to the register.
required.rationale: Registering '' or null makes a later blank row DUPLICATE instead of INVALID.

required.check: The duplicate register stores and compares the raw receipt_id (no trim/upperCase), so 'R' and ' R ' are distinct.
required.rationale: Trimming before lookup marks ' R ' (row 4) DUPLICATE and loses group A's winner.

required.check: The first occurrence of a usable id is added to the register before the void/amount checks, even when it is voided or has a null/non-positive amount.
required.rationale: Registering only eligible ids lets the second 'R' (row 3, amount 10) become ELIGIBLE/WINNER instead of DUPLICATE.

required.check: A later occurrence of a registered id gets DUPLICATE before any void/amount test and can never become the winner.
required.rationale: Checking eligibility first labels row 3 WINNER.

required.check: A first occurrence is a candidate only if voided is false and amount is non-null and > 0 (null checked before comparing); otherwise it gets INELIGIBLE.
required.rationale: Comparing a null amount without a guard or ignoring voided accepts rows 2 and 7.

required.check: The first candidate of the group gets WINNER and is remembered; later candidates get ELIGIBLE and do not replace it.
required.rationale: A 'latest wins' or 'largest wins' rule replaces ' R ' (2.00) with X (4.00).

required.check: Each output-0 row copies the input receipt (`$out.0.* = $in.0.*` or per field), adds its disposition, and sets rows_seen to the inclusive running count of the group's records so far.
required.rationale: Using the final group size or a 0-based count gives wrong rows_seen on interim rows.

required.check: winner_receipt on output-0 rows is the winner's raw id once a winner exists (including on the WINNER row itself) and null before that; the winner-id variable is explicitly set to null at group start (a bare `string` global starts as "", not null).
required.rationale: A bare-declared winner id yields "" instead of null on the INVALID/INELIGIBLE rows before the winner.

required.check: Output 1 is emitted only when the group has a winner (`finishGroup` returns false or `transform` returns SKIP otherwise) and copies the chosen receipt's fields saved when it was selected, with disposition CHOSEN, winner_receipt = its own raw id and rows_seen = final group size.
required.rationale: Copying `$in.0` in transform gives the last receipt's context (row 5) instead of the chosen one (row 4).

required.check: Global (non-accumulator) state is reset per group, e.g. in `initGroup`: the id register list is cleared and the winner flag/id cleared. Accumulator fields are reset from metadata automatically, so an explicit accumulator reset is optional.
required.rationale: Without clearing the register, ids from group A would mark group B rows DUPLICATE and A's winner would leak into B.

forbidden.check: Returns ALL (or otherwise sends the same annotated record to both outputs) from `updateTransform` or `transform`.
forbidden.rationale: Clause 7 forbids broadcasting; output 1 must hold only the chosen receipt.

forbidden.check: Emits interim winner records on output 1 from `updateTransform` (e.g. returning 1 when a new winner is found).
forbidden.rationale: Output 1 must carry exactly one final CHOSEN row per group with a winner.

T57.notes: Accumulator metadata (n, accepted, has_winner) is reset from metadata each group, so items accept code that never resets it explicitly; global variables (seen_ids list, winner id/flag) must still be reset manually.

required.check: Denormalizer contract: `append()` processes every record of the warehouse group into list state; `transform()` runs once per group and writes one summary to `$out.0`, including for a group with no survivors.
required.rationale: Emitting only when a winner exists drops the empty warehouse B.

required.check: Context fields are saved from the first record of the group (flag or count == 0) and written from that saved copy, including nullable context_value and unused_archive_label; not from `$in.0` in transform() (the last record).
required.rationale: Copying `$in.0` in transform() writes source_row 7 instead of 1 for warehouse A.

required.check: rows_seen counts every input record, incremented before any early return for ignored rows (bad slot, unknown op, malformed units, repeated removes).
required.rationale: Counting after the guards reports 6 instead of 7 for warehouse A.

required.check: A row is ignored for state (but still counted) when slot_id is null or blank after trim, or when operation is not exactly "ADD" or "REMOVE" (case-sensitive, null-safe `==`); usable slot ids keep their raw spelling in comparisons and evidence.
required.rationale: Upper-casing operations or trimming ids changes which rows count as ADD/REMOVE.

required.check: REMOVE deletes every earlier retained addition with the same raw slot_id from all parallel lists (iterating backwards, or rebuilding the lists), not just the first or last match.
required.rationale: Removing a single match leaves one of S's two additions alive in warehouse A.

required.check: A REMOVE does not block later ADDs of that slot (no permanent tombstone set); removing an unknown slot is a no-op.
required.rationale: A tombstone set drops the re-added S 3.50 that must appear in the evidence.

required.check: An ADD is retained only if the trimmed units_txt fully matches 1–9 digits with an optional '.' and 1–2 digits (e.g. `~= "[0-9]{1,9}(\\.[0-9]{1,2})?"`) checked before `str2decimal`, and the parsed value is > 0; null, blank, signs, exponent and malformed text are ignored without throwing.
required.rationale: `str2decimal` on 'bad:date' or '' throws and fails the graph.

required.check: The winner has the greatest units; ties keep the earlier addition unless a timestamp rule decides (strict comparisons, no >= replacement).
required.rationale: Picking the last or first survivor ignores units ranking.

required.check: Among equal units, a non-null observed_at beats null, and between two non-null values the later full date-time wins (pre-epoch and midnight are real times).
required.rationale: Warehouse A's three survivors all have 3.50 units, so only these timestamp rules select T at 2026-01-01 over S (1960) and T (null).

required.check: chosen_slot, chosen_at, chosen_units and chosen_cost are all taken from the same surviving addition (same list index), chosen_cost unranked and possibly null/negative; with no survivors all four are null and no list is indexed.
required.rationale: Indexing an empty list throws; mixing indices pairs one slot's units with another's cost.

required.check: surviving_slots is every retained addition's raw slot_id in arrival order, including repeats, joined with "," (`join(",", slots)` or concatenation without a trailing comma), and "" when there are none.
required.rationale: Deduplicating or listing only the winner gives 'S,T' or 'T' instead of 'S,T,T'.

required.check: All per-group state — the retained lists, the count and the first-record flag — is reset for the next warehouse in `clean()` or at the end of `transform()`.
required.rationale: Without the reset, warehouse B inherits A's survivors and count.

forbidden.check: Keeps only a running best candidate (single winner variables) instead of the retained additions, so retracting the current best cannot fall back to the remaining ones.
forbidden.rationale: Warehouse A's best (S 9) is removed later; the correct winner comes from the remaining evidence.

forbidden.check: Writes summary fields to `$out.0` inside `append()` and relies on them for output (assignments in append() have no effect).
forbidden.rationale: The emitted summary would be empty.

required.check: Two-output Reformat contract: `transform()` returns SKIP for an unchanged existing account, 1 for a new account (opening only), and ALL for a changed existing account (closing on port 0 and opening on port 1).
required.rationale: Returning ALL for a new account also emits an unfilled port-0 close; returning 1 for a change loses the close.

required.check: 'New account' is decided by `previous_sk` being null (`isnull($in.0.previous_sk)` or `== null`), not by the attribute or previous_value nulls.
required.rationale: Testing previous_risk_class/previous_value for null misclassifies existing accounts with null prior attributes (D, F).

required.check: 'Changed' compares risk_class with previous_risk_class and contract_value with previous_value using null-safe `!=` (or explicit null handling), without nvl/trim normalisation, so null vs "" and null vs 0.00 are changes and null vs null is not.
required.rationale: nvl/isBlank normalisation hides the null→"" (F) and null→0.00 (D row 6) changes.

required.check: A new account always opens, even when both incoming attributes are null (the existence test comes before or overrides the unchanged test).
required.rationale: Comparing two nulls first makes the all-null new account A row 1 look unchanged and drops it.

required.check: An unchanged existing account returns SKIP before any `sequence(...).next()` call.
required.rationale: Allocating before the decision consumes 900000-series keys for rows that emit nothing.

required.check: The closing record (port 0) has version_sk = previous_sk, valid_from = previous_from, valid_to = event_at exactly (no day/second subtraction) and is_current = false.
required.rationale: Any adjustment of valid_to breaks the half-open boundary required by clause 6.

required.check: The closing record carries previous_risk_class and previous_value, not the incoming risk_class/contract_value.
required.rationale: Copy-through alone leaves the new values on the close (expected LOW/2.00 for B).

required.check: The opening record (port 1) carries the incoming risk_class/contract_value with valid_from = event_at, valid_to = null and is_current = true.
required.rationale: Leaving the copied placeholders produces a wrong window on the opened version.

required.check: The opening's version_sk comes from exactly one `next()` on the graph sequence DimKeys per opening (`sequence(DimKeys,long).next()`, or `sequence(DimKeys).next()` widened to the long field), with no CTL counter and no `reset()`.
required.rationale: A local counter or a second next() per record gives keys that do not match 900000, 900001, ….

required.check: Both emitted records copy the other common fields from the input (`$out.N.* = $in.0.*` or per field) and then overwrite version_sk, valid_from, valid_to and is_current, preserving nullable context, unused_archive_label and notes such as BAD:DATE unparsed.
required.rationale: Skipping the overwrite emits the input placeholders (version_sk 0, valid_from 2026-01-01) as real values.

forbidden.check: Returns STOP (or raises an error) for unchanged or unexpected events instead of SKIP.
forbidden.rationale: STOP aborts the graph; unchanged events must simply emit nothing.

forbidden.check: Keeps its own cross-row state (map, previous-key or last-version variables) to decide prior versions instead of using each event's previous_* fields.
forbidden.rationale: Clause 7 says the resolver supplies the prior version per event and forbids a reconciliation buffer.

T59.notes: Prompt states DimKeys is a 'long sequence' and asks for a 'long surrogate' but does not name the typed call; item .9 accepts both `sequence(DimKeys,long).next()` and `sequence(DimKeys).next()` (integer widened, values ~900000 fit). If the owner wants the typed form required, tighten .9. Old T59.6/.9 restated .3/.2 and were removed.

required.check: Normalizer contract: `count()` returns the number of ledger rows for the request (0 for a silent unchanged request) and `transform(integer idx)` builds row idx on the single output `$out.0`.
required.rationale: A fixed count or SKIP-based filtering emits wrong numbers of rows per request.

required.check: request_kind == "CANCEL" (exact) is tested before any rate validation, and new_rate_txt is ignored on cancellation (no regex test or str2decimal on it).
required.rationale: Validating first turns cancellation D ('BAD:DATE') into an ERROR row.

required.check: A cancellation with previous_sk emits CLOSE then CANCELLED (CANCELLED carrying previous_sk, previous_from, valid_to = event_at and previous_rate); without previous_sk it emits only CANCELLED with null version_sk, valid_from, valid_to and rate; it is emitted regardless of audit_requested and allocates no PriceKeys value. (is_current on CANCELLED is not graded.)
required.rationale: Gating CANCELLED on audit_requested drops the always-required audit row for D, E and I.

required.check: For a non-cancel request, null or blank (after trim) new_rate_txt means an unpriced tariff with rate null — not an error.
required.rationale: Treating blank as malformed turns request F into ERROR instead of UNCHANGED.

required.check: Non-blank rate text must fully match 1–8 digits with an optional '.' and 1–2 digits (e.g. `~= "[0-9]{1,8}(\\.[0-9]{1,2})?"` on the trimmed text) before `str2decimal`; signs, exponent (1e2) and commas fail.
required.rationale: `str2decimal("1e2")` may succeed, so parsing first accepts request G instead of rejecting it.

required.check: A malformed rate produces exactly one row (count 1): record_kind ERROR, audit_note BAD_RATE, version_sk/valid_from/valid_to/rate null, with no version rows and no key allocation.
required.rationale: Emitting versions or a second row for a bad rate breaks the ledger contract.

required.check: An existing tariff is unchanged when the parsed rate equals previous_rate under null-safe equality (null == null unchanged; 0 vs null changed).
required.rationale: A non-null-safe compare makes F (null vs null) a change and H ('0' vs null) unchanged.

required.check: An unchanged tariff emits nothing (count 0) when audit_requested is false, and one UNCHANGED row when true, carrying previous_sk, previous_from, previous_rate and valid_to null. (is_current on UNCHANGED is not graded.)
required.rationale: Always emitting UNCHANGED creates audit rows nobody asked for (request B).

required.check: A replacement emits CLOSE first — version_sk previous_sk, valid_from previous_from, valid_to event_at (no subtraction), is_current false, rate previous_rate — then OPEN; a new tariff (no previous_sk) emits only OPEN, even with a null rate.
required.rationale: Reversed order or a CLOSE for a new tariff corrupts the version ledger.

required.check: OPEN takes exactly one PriceKeys value — `sequence(PriceKeys,long).next()` once per opening, in `count()` (saved to a variable) or in `transform()` at the OPEN index — with valid_from event_at, valid_to null, is_current true and the parsed rate.
required.rationale: Calling next() per row or per transform call skips keys (expected 1000, 1001, 1002).

required.check: When audit_requested is true for a new or changed tariff, a REPRICED row follows the version rows and carries the same new version fields, reusing the OPEN key (saved variable or `sequence(PriceKeys,long).current()`).
required.rationale: A fresh next() for the audit copy gives REPRICED a key different from its OPEN.

required.check: Per-request preparation state (flags, parsed rate, new key, count) is recomputed or reset at the start of each `count()` (or in `clean()`), so a malformed or silent request does not reuse the previous request's rate or key.
required.rationale: A stale parsed rate or new key from request C would leak into later rows.

forbidden.check: Allocates a PriceKeys value for a cancellation, an ERROR, an unchanged request or a CLOSE row.
forbidden.rationale: Clause 3/8 forbid it, and it shifts every subsequent key.

forbidden.check: Returns STOP or calls `raiseError` for a malformed rate instead of emitting the ERROR row.
forbidden.rationale: The spec requires a defined ERROR/BAD_RATE ledger row, not an aborted graph.

T60.notes: is_current on CANCELLED and UNCHANGED audit rows is not specified by the prompt (reference writes false on CANCELLED-with-previous, null without, true on UNCHANGED) — items do not grade it; consider specifying it. Typed `sequence(PriceKeys,long)` is the only form listed because the prompt calls it a long sequence; `.current()` for the REPRICED row is accepted.

required.check: Two-output Reformat contract: `transform()` keeps the accepted state in global variables across calls and returns SKIP for an unchanged row, 1 for an opening only (no current version), and ALL for a change (close on port 0 + open on port 1).
required.rationale: Returning ALL without a current version emits an unfilled close; returning 1 on a change loses the close.

required.check: A new key is detected by comparing business_ref with the saved previous key using explicit presence — a boolean flag, a row counter, or a key variable explicitly initialised to null (`string prev = null;`, valid because business_ref is non-nullable) — so a first key "" is still seen as new.
required.rationale: A bare `string prev;` starts as "" and equals the empty first key, so its seed/state initialisation is skipped.

required.check: Seed fields are read only on the first row of a key: a non-null seed_sk sets the current version to (seed_sk, seed_from, seed_region, seed_fee); a null seed_sk means no current version.
required.rationale: Ignoring the seed on key A's first row opens a new version instead of recognising E/5.00 as unchanged.

required.check: On later rows of the same key the seed fields are ignored and comparisons use the state accepted by the component.
required.rationale: Comparing with the stale seed (999/STALE/9.00 on row 2) produces a spurious change.

required.check: The change test compares region_cd and service_fee with the saved current values using null-safe `!=` (or explicit null handling): null == null, "" ≠ null and 0 ≠ null.
required.rationale: nvl-style normalisation hides the null→"" change on row 3.

required.check: An unchanged row (current version exists, no change) returns SKIP without calling GeoKeys and without updating the saved context, attributes, key or start date.
required.rationale: Updating the saved context on silent row 2 makes the later close carry r2 instead of r1.

required.check: When no current version exists the row opens even if both attributes are null.
required.rationale: Treating null/null as 'unchanged' against default state drops the first opening (key "" row 1).

required.check: Each opening uses exactly one `sequence(GeoKeys,long).next()` (or `sequence(GeoKeys).next()` widened to the long field) and sets version_sk to it, valid_from = effective_at, valid_to = null, is_current = true, with the current input's context (`$out.1.* = $in.0.*`).
required.rationale: A second next() for a change pair, or a local counter, breaks the 3000, 3001, … key sequence.

required.check: The closing record (port 0) uses the saved current version_sk, saved start date as valid_from, saved region_cd/service_fee, valid_to = the incoming effective_at exactly, and is_current = false.
required.rationale: Putting the incoming attributes or a shifted valid_to on the close breaks the half-open history.

required.check: The closing record's context fields come from the saved row that introduced the current version (the seed row, or the row that opened it), including notes and unused_archive_label — not from the current input.
required.rationale: Copy-through of `$in.0` on the close writes r5 instead of r4 on A's first close.

required.check: After every opening the component saves that row's full context, attributes, new key and effective_at as the current version.
required.rationale: Not saving the opening makes the next change close the seed again (A row 6 must close 3002).

required.check: When business_ref changes, the whole current-version state is re-initialised from the new key's first row (seed or none), even if the previous key's first row was silent.
required.rationale: Leaking key A's version into key B closes a version B never had.

forbidden.check: Uses an uninitialised (bare-declared) previous-key or saved-attribute variable tested with `== null`/`isnull()` or against "" as the 'no state yet' sentinel (declared strings start as "", and "" is a valid key here).
forbidden.rationale: The first key "" is then mistaken for already-initialised state.

forbidden.check: Copies the current input into the closing record (`$out.0.* = $in.0.*`) without restoring the saved context and attributes.
forbidden.rationale: The close must describe the previously accepted version, not the incoming event.

T61.notes: Old T61.8 (UTC/half-open/notes) was free and dropped; the exact valid_to boundary is folded into .9. GeoKeys typed vs untyped call: both accepted (see T59 note).

required.check: Rollup contract: all five functions are defined; `updateGroup` accumulates and returns false (or `updateTransform` returns SKIP) so nothing is emitted per record; `finishGroup` returns true; `transform(counter, acc)` — called with counter 0, 1, … until SKIP — writes one summary at counter 0 and returns SKIP for counter > 0.
required.rationale: Without the counter guard the summary is emitted repeatedly; an emitting updateTransform adds per-record rows the spec does not want.

required.check: period_label is the group month formatted yyyy-MM in UTC: `date2str(d, "yyyy-MM", locale, "UTC")` or `getYear(d,"UTC")`/`getMonth(d,"UTC")` (any record of the group may be used); date functions without a timezone use the host zone (CET).
required.rationale: Host-timezone formatting shifts events near midnight UTC on the 1st/last day into the wrong month.

required.check: The first event's context (claim_ref_no, source_row_no, operator_note, unused_archive_label and the other base fields) is saved when the group starts (`initGroup`, or a first-record flag reset per group) into globals or accumulator fields and written to the summary — not taken from `$in.0` in transform().
required.rationale: Copying `$in.0` in transform() gives a later claim's claim_ref_no/source_row_no.

required.check: A null amount_override_txt (and only null) falls back to net_amount, which may itself be null.
required.rationale: Falling back on blank text lets claim-4 contribute 1.00 instead of counting as bad.

required.check: A non-null override is trimmed and must fully match an optional '-', 1–10 digits and an optional '.' with 1–2 digits (e.g. `~= "-?[0-9]{1,10}(\\.[0-9]{1,2})?"`) before `str2decimal`; '+', exponent (1e2), 3 decimals (1.005) and date text fail.
required.rationale: `str2decimal("")` throws and '1e2'/'1.005' would be accepted by a parse-only approach.

required.check: A failed override increments bad_amount_rows and contributes no amount to any bucket or average, even when net_amount is usable.
required.rationale: Falling back to net_amount adds claim-2's 200.00 to pending.

required.check: paid_total/pending_total add usable non-null effective amounts only for status_cd exactly "PAID"/"PENDING" (case-sensitive, null-safe `==`); other statuses add nothing and negative amounts reduce the bucket.
required.rationale: Case-insensitive matching adds claim-10 ('paid') to paid_total.

required.check: billable_average = sum / count of usable non-null amounts on billable rows regardless of status (zero and negative included), as decimal division rounded with `round(x, 2)` (half away from zero), and null when the count is 0.
required.rationale: Restricting to PAID/PENDING or returning 0 for an empty population gives wrong values for groups A and B (48.75 / null).

required.check: A row is late iff delay_days is non-null, > 2 and late_waived is false; bad-amount rows are classified too.
required.rationale: Skipping bad-amount rows loses claim-2's late flag in the 2-of-6 fraction.

required.check: late_percent = round(100 × late / rows_seen, 2) using decimal division over every row of the group (e.g. `100D * late / n`).
required.rationale: Dividing by valid-amount rows instead of rows_seen changes 33.33.

required.check: reopened_rows counts rows whose immediately preceding row in the group had status exactly PAID and whose own status is exactly PENDING; the predecessor status is updated on every row regardless of amount validity, billability or waiver.
required.rationale: Updating the predecessor only on valid rows miscounts A's two PAID→PENDING transitions.

required.check: Per-group state kept in globals — predecessor presence/status, the first-context capture flag and saved context — is reset at the start of each group (`initGroup`) so the first event has no predecessor; accumulator fields are reset from metadata, so an explicit accumulator reset is optional.
required.rationale: A leaked PAID predecessor from group A makes group B's first PENDING a reopen (expected 1, not 2).

forbidden.check: Computes late_percent or billable_average with integer division (e.g. `100 * late / n` on integers, then round).
forbidden.rationale: Integer division gives 33 instead of 33.33 for the 1-in-3 fraction.

forbidden.check: Uses `number`/double (e.g. `str2double`, number variables) for the amount sums or the mean.
forbidden.rationale: Double arithmetic loses the exact half-up rounding the spec asks for on decimal amounts.

T62.notes: Fixture events are all at 2026-01-01 00:00 UTC, which is still January in CET, so the UTC requirement in .2 is checked by reading only.

required.check: Rollup contract: all five functions are defined; `updateGroup` accumulates and returns false (no per-record output); `finishGroup` decides whether the group emits; `transform(counter, acc)` — called with counter 0, 1, … until SKIP — writes one summary at counter 0 and returns SKIP for counter > 0.
required.rationale: Missing finishGroup or the counter guard emits nothing or duplicates the summary.

required.check: The first valuation's context fields and its audit_required are saved when the group starts (`initGroup`, or a first-record flag reset per group) and written/used from that saved copy; later audit_required values are ignored.
required.rationale: Using a later row's audit_required (B row 7 = true) emits group B, which must be suppressed.

required.check: A row is eligible only if quote_currency == currency_cd (exact), coverage_days is non-null and > 0, and asset_value is non-null; otherwise it counts in excluded_rows.
required.rationale: Missing the coverage_days > 0 check lets B row 7 (0 days) in.

required.check: haircut_txt is examined only after the row passed the currency/days/value checks, so excluded rows' garbage (BAD:DATE, 'bad') is never parsed.
required.rationale: Parsing first makes `str2decimal("BAD:DATE")` on the USD row throw.

required.check: For an eligible row, null or blank (after trim) haircut_txt means a 0 % haircut.
required.rationale: Treating blank as invalid excludes A row 3 (−3.00) and changes the average.

required.check: A non-blank haircut must fully match 1–3 digits with an optional '.' and 1–2 digits (e.g. `~= "[0-9]{1,3}(\\.[0-9]{1,2})?"`) before `str2decimal`, and the value must be ≤ 100; otherwise the row is excluded (excluded_rows +1) without throwing.
required.rationale: Skipping the range check accepts 100.01 (A row 5) as a negative-value haircut.

required.check: Each eligible row adds coverage_days to weighted_days and asset_value × (100 − haircut) / 100 × coverage_days to the decimal weighted total, including negative asset values.
required.rationale: Excluding the negative A row 3 (−3.00) gives 10.000 instead of 6.750 for group A.

required.check: adjusted_average = round(weighted_total / weighted_days, 3) with decimal division, and null when weighted_days is 0.
required.rationale: Dividing by eligible_rows instead of weighted_days ignores the day weighting the spec requires.

required.check: high_share = round(100 × days of rows with risk_grade exactly "HIGH" / weighted_days, 2) (case-sensitive, null-safe), and 0 when weighted_days is 0.
required.rationale: Counting 'high' (A row 3) or leaving high_share null on an empty population is wrong.

required.check: A group with no eligible rows is emitted (adjusted_average null, high_share 0) only when the saved first audit_required is true; otherwise `finishGroup` returns false (or transform returns SKIP).
required.rationale: Emitting all empty groups outputs B; suppressing all drops C.

required.check: fiscal_period maps months to the April fiscal year: Apr–Jun Q1, Jul–Sep Q2, Oct–Dec Q3, Jan–Mar Q4 of the previous starting year, formatted '<year>-Q<n>' (e.g. 2026-Q1, 2025-Q4), using calendar year/month not ISO week-year.
required.rationale: Using the calendar quarter or the event's own year for Jan–Mar mislabels 2025-Q4 and 2026-Q3.

required.check: The year and month for fiscal_period are taken in UTC (`getMonth(d,"UTC")`/`getYear(d,"UTC")` or `date2str(d, ..., "UTC")`), since date functions without a timezone use the host zone (CET).
required.rationale: In CET, 2026-03-31 23:30 UTC (group A's first row) becomes April and yields 2026-Q1 instead of 2025-Q4.

forbidden.check: Computes high_share or adjusted_average with integer division (e.g. `100 * high_days / days` on integers).
forbidden.rationale: Integer division truncates 25.00-style shares and averages.

forbidden.check: Uses `number`/double (e.g. `str2double`, number variables) for the haircut or the weighted total.
forbidden.rationale: Clause 5 requires exact decimal arithmetic throughout.

T63.notes: Accumulator fields are reset from metadata each group, so explicit acc resets are optional; the saved first-row globals (context, first audit flag) must be re-captured per group (item .2). The host-timezone trap is exercised by group A's first row (2026-03-31 23:30 UTC).
